title: Compact incident digest carousel — one-click postmortem, runbook snippets, and token-cost attribution
creator: Priya Raman
description: Design a compact, horizontally-scrollable incident digest carousel for the Redwood Console incident detail panel. The digest presents 3–5 micro-tiles summarizing the incident: correlated metric snapshot, top failing routes, quick-runbook snippets, estimated token-cost impact for the window, and a one-click Postmortem link that pre-populates postmortem metadata. Goal: reduce cognitive load during triage, speed handoffs, and surface cost signals tied to recent anomalous traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Carousel renders as a compact horizontal strip within the incident detail view without increasing vertical height by more than 160px.
Each tile contains: title, 3-line summary (auto-generated), one contextual CTA (Open Runbook / Jump to Trace / Open Postmortem draft), and a tiny sparkline or single stat.
One-click Postmortem CTA opens the postmortem composer with incident metadata (time window, SLO(s) affected, primary alert rule, assignee) filled in and a short prompt for the lead engineer.
Runbook snippets show first 120 characters and an Expand action; copy-to-clipboard available for commands.
Token-cost estimate shows an aggregated token delta (token estimate and USD range) for the incident window and links to cost-breakdown route in Console.
Design annotated with responsive behaviour for narrow panes and keyboard accessibility for carousel navigation.
Prototype validated with 4 engineers/oncall participants in a moderated usability session with >=80% success on ‘create postmortem’ flow and ‘find relevant runbook’ task.
comments: 2026-02-26 Priya Raman: Initial ticket created. Problem statement: during high-severity incidents the incident detail page is dense; oncall engineers often need to open multiple tabs (metrics, runbooks, cost) which slows triage. Proposal: a compact digest carousel to surface the most actionable bits inline.

2026-02-28 Ethan Cole: Sketched three tile variants (metric-first, runbook-first, cost-first). Prefer metric-first for first iteration since SLO/context is the most frequent entry point. Attached figma with variants.

2026-03-02 Mei Zhang (SRE): Suggest including a 'confidence' indicator on token-cost estimate — some requests are batched and token estimation can be noisy. Also call out when estimate is based on sampled logs.

2026-03-04 Product Review: PM Andres Soto — positive for one-click postmortem but ask that the composer allow users to remove or edit auto-filled metadata. Also request telemetry event names for 'digest.tile_clicked' and 'postmortem.prefill_accepted'.

2026-03-05 UX Research: Ran 5 quick guerrilla tests with oncall engineers. Findings: (1) Postmortem prefill saved ~40s on average, (2) Runbook snippets need clearer affordance for 'execute' vs 'edit', (3) Carousel navigation arrows were missed when the user is focused on the timeline — recommend subtle focus ring and keyboard shortcuts (< and >). Full notes in notion link.

2026-03-07 Engineering sync (Ethan & infra team): Feasibility notes: runbook snippet content must be sanitized for display (strip long scripts), need an API extension to return cost estimates per-incident window (ENG dependency queued). We also flagged potential perf issue rendering sparklines — will use canvas-based micro-sparkline component.

2026-03-09 Design review: Spike prototype demoed to stakeholders; minor visual polish requested: reduce badge saturation for cost estimate, add microcopy hint about estimated vs exact cost, and ensure color-blind friendly palette for sparkline deltas.

2026-03-10 Ethan Cole: Updated prototype in Figma (link above). Created ENG dependency ticket ENG-22012 for cost-aggregation endpoint and ENG-22047 for postmortem composer API. Marking this ticket In Review and requesting Handoff doc for implementation.
2026-03-10 Priya Raman: Next steps: (1) finalize accessibility spec, (2) produce handoff tokens and spacing scale, (3) schedule prototype QA with SREs during next oncall rotation (2026-03-16).
